# Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Agent Observability (Part 1)

Patterns

metadata.breadcrumb: Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Agent Observability

document:
# Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Agent Observability (Part 2)

Where to look What good looks like Agentforce | Session Tracing ✅ Use the native Session Tracing Data Model (STDM) capturing agent interactions in a unified data model on Data 360 rather than building a parallel telemetry system — recording each conversation as a trace hierarchy of sessions, interactions (turns), and steps (UserInputStep, LLMExecutionStep, FunctionStep) Agentforce | Session Tracing ✅ Rely on the standard STDM objects (AIAgentSession, AIAgentSessionParticipant, AIAgentInteraction, AIAgentInteractionStep, AIAgentInteractionMessage), which capture actions natively as interaction steps rather than requiring a separate action log Agentforce | Session Tracing ✅ Retrieve token usage, model, and prompt details by joining interaction steps to their LLM-call records (via GenerationId and GenAiGatewayRequest/Response references) rather than storing them as custom session fields Agentforce | Session Tracing ✅ Capture reasoning traces from the Atlas Reasoning Engine — Session Tracing records the planner’s steps as part of each interaction — to reveal agent decision processes and improve debuggability Agentforce | Agent Configuration ✅ Log turn-level details including user input, agent response, reasoning explanation, confidence scores, retrieved context, actions attempted, and errors encountered Einstein | Trust Layer ✅ Turn on the Einstein Trust Layer generative AI audit trail (prompt and response text, PII-masked versions, grounding data, safety and toxicity scores, model details) streamed to Data 360, plus Einstein Generative AI and Feedback Data Collection and Storage for long-term retention Platform | Custom Objects ✅ Reserve custom logging objects for deliberate exceptions — such as a lightweight object correlating agent behavior with business outcomes — rather than making them the primary logging substrate Platform | Dashboard ✅ Correlate agent behavior with business outcomes, identify improvement opportunities through pattern analysis, and feed continuous learning pipelines with quality-labeled examples

metadata.breadcrumb: Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Agent Observability

document:
# Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Agent Observability (Part 3)

Anti-Patterns

Where to look What bad looks like Platform | Custom Objects ⚠️ Hand-building custom transactional objects as the primary conversation-logging substrate instead of the native Session Tracing Data Model, running into scale problems storing multi-turn conversations, large JSON payloads, and rapid data growth Agentforce | Session Tracing ⚠️ Building a parallel telemetry system when Agentforce Session Tracing already captures interactions in a unified data model on Data 360 Agentforce | Agent Configuration ⚠️ Logging only agent responses without capturing inputs, reasoning traces, retrieved context, and actions taken Einstein | Trust Layer ⚠️ Disabling the Einstein Trust Layer audit trail in production or not turning on Feedback Data Collection and Storage for long-term retention in Data 360 Platform | Monitoring ⚠️ Relying solely on conversation success/failure without capturing token usage, model, and prompt details through the STDM LLM-call joins

metadata.breadcrumb: Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Agent Observability

document:
# Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Performance Monitoring (Part 1)

Patterns

metadata.breadcrumb: Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Performance Monitoring

document:
# Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Performance Monitoring (Part 2)

Where to look What good looks like Platform | Monitoring ✅ Measure response latency at percentiles (p50, p95, p99) revealing typical performance and worst-case experiences Platform | Monitoring ✅ Instrument each latency phase separately (model inference, context retrieval, action execution, network) enabling targeted optimization Platform | Monitoring ✅ Alert when p95 latency exceeds thresholds indicating performance degradation Platform | Monitoring ✅ Track token distribution (prompt tokens, completion tokens, total tokens) per conversation, per agent, and per use case Platform | Monitoring ✅ Detect outlier conversations consuming excessive tokens suggesting prompt issues or misuse Platform | Monitoring ✅ Compare current throughput against known rate limits or capacity baselines alerting when approaching thresholds Platform | Monitoring ✅ Calculate error rates as percentage of total requests enabling comparison across agents and time periods Platform | Monitoring ✅ Distinguish between error categories (model errors, permission errors, integration errors) requiring different responses Platform | Monitoring ✅ Calculate availability as percentage of time agents successfully respond to requests and track against SLOs Platform | Proactive Monitoring ✅ Configure Proactive Monitoring thresholds based on baseline agent behavior patterns rather than accepting defaults Platform | Scale Center ✅ Review Scale Center data after deploying new agents or making significant prompt changes validating resource consumption matches expectations

metadata.breadcrumb: Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Performance Monitoring

document:
# Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Performance Monitoring (Part 3)

Anti-Patterns

Where to look What bad looks like Platform | Monitoring ⚠️ Measuring only average latency instead of percentiles, masking worst-case user experiences Platform | Monitoring ⚠️ Tracking total latency without instrumenting individual phases (inference, retrieval, action execution) Platform | Monitoring ⚠️ Treating all errors the same rather than categorizing by type (model, permission, integration) for appropriate response Platform | Proactive Monitoring ⚠️ Accepting default Proactive Monitoring thresholds without tuning to baseline agent behavior patterns Platform | Scale Center ⚠️ Deploying new agents or making prompt changes without reviewing Scale Center data to validate resource consumption Platform | Monitoring ⚠️ Ignoring token consumption patterns and failing to detect outlier conversations consuming 10x typical tokens

metadata.breadcrumb: Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Performance Monitoring

document:
# Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Quality Metrics and Evaluation (Part 1)

Patterns

metadata.breadcrumb: Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Quality Metrics and Evaluation

document:
# Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Quality Metrics and Evaluation (Part 2)

Where to look What good looks like Agentforce | Testing Center ✅ Start with native testing and evaluation tooling: maintain reusable test-case sets in Agentforce Testing Center and run agents against them in batch, checking whether the agent selected the expected topic and action and produced an acceptable response Agentforce | Testing Center ✅ Use native evaluators — out-of-the-box quality dimensions and the LLM-as-judge approach for scoring conversational quality — and author custom evaluators for organization-specific criteria, using representative conversations so evaluation reflects real usage Agentforce | Testing Center ✅ For factual questions with known answers, maintain known-answer assertions as repeatable test cases in Testing Center; for open-ended questions, add human review of sampled conversations Data 360 | Retrieval Quality ✅ For agents grounded in a knowledge base, use native retrieval-quality analysis to assess context relevance, answer relevance, and faithfulness (groundedness) of responses Einstein | Trust Layer ✅ Rely on the Einstein Trust Layer runtime toxicity detection as the first line of guardrail defense, then improve safety monitoring through content filtering, manual review sampling, user reporting, and fairness audits across demographic groups Data 360 | GenAIFeedback ✅ Capture user satisfaction through Agentforce feedback flowing into the GenAIFeedback / GenAIFeedbackDetail DMOs in Data 360 (thumbs-up/down, accept/reject, edits, verbatim comments) alongside gateway request and generation data Platform | Analytics ✅ Combine explicit feedback (asked before escalation, after conversation, follow-up surveys) with implicit signals (completion rates, escalation, abandonment, retries), correlating with conversation characteristics to guide improvement prioritization

metadata.breadcrumb: Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Quality Metrics and Evaluation

document:
# Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Quality Metrics and Evaluation (Part 3)

Anti-Patterns

Where to look What bad looks like Agentforce | Testing Center ⚠️ Building and running a custom test harness instead of starting with Agentforce Testing Center’s reusable test sets and native evaluators Agentforce | Testing Center ⚠️ Relying solely on automated evaluation without human review for quality assessment of open-ended responses Platform | Monitoring ⚠️ Monitoring only accuracy without tracking relevance, safety, and user satisfaction dimensions Data 360 | GenAIFeedback ⚠️ Failing to collect any user feedback (explicit or implicit) on agent response quality when Agentforce feedback already flows into the GenAIFeedback DMOs Agentforce | Agent Configuration ⚠️ Skipping fairness audits assessing outcome distributions across demographic groups

metadata.breadcrumb: Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Quality Metrics and Evaluation

document:
# Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Model Drift Detection

Patterns

Where to look What good looks like Agentforce | Agent Configuration ✅ Establish baseline performance immediately after agent deployment measuring accuracy, relevance, safety, and satisfaction across representative test cases Agentforce | Agent Configuration ✅ Periodically re-evaluate against the same test cases revealing performance changes independent of usage pattern shifts Platform | Monitoring ✅ Alert when quality metrics decline beyond acceptable thresholds defined by business impact tolerance Platform | Analytics ✅ Monitor input characteristics (question length, topic distribution, language complexity, domain terminology) detecting significant distribution shifts Platform | Monitoring ✅ Monitor response characteristics (average response length, action invocation rates, escalation frequencies, error patterns) establishing behavioral baselines Platform | Monitoring ✅ Configure automated alerts firing when drift metrics exceed thresholds triggering investigation and remediation

Anti-Patterns

Where to look What bad looks like Agentforce | Agent Configuration ⚠️ Failing to establish baseline performance after initial agent deployment, making drift undetectable Platform | Monitoring ⚠️ Ignoring distribution drift when user input patterns change significantly from what agents were designed to handle Platform | Monitoring ⚠️ Not monitoring behavioral changes (response length, action rates, escalation frequencies) against established baselines Platform | Monitoring ⚠️ Having no automated alerting for drift metrics, relying only on manual observation to detect degradation

metadata.breadcrumb: Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Model Drift Detection

document:
# Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Anomaly Detection and Alerting

Patterns

Where to look What good looks like Platform | Monitoring ✅ Monitor token consumption distributions detecting outlier conversations and investigate those consuming 10x typical tokens Platform | Monitoring ✅ Detect sudden increases in failure rates, new error types not in baseline, or localized error concentrations affecting specific users or agents Platform | Analytics ✅ Track conversation abandonment by conversation stage identifying whether users abandon during initial interaction, mid-conversation, or after task completion Platform | Monitoring ✅ Route critical agent failures to on-call engineers immediately, quality degradation to product teams during business hours, and minor anomalies to daily digests

Anti-Patterns

Where to look What bad looks like Platform | Monitoring ⚠️ Treating all alerts with equal urgency, causing alert fatigue and missed critical failures Platform | Monitoring ⚠️ Ignoring cost anomalies like token consumption spikes that may indicate prompt issues, abuse, or infrastructure problems Platform | Analytics ⚠️ Not tracking conversation abandonment rates or failing to analyze abandonment by stage Platform | Monitoring ⚠️ Waiting for user reports rather than proactively detecting error rate spikes through automated monitoring

metadata.breadcrumb: Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Anomaly Detection and Alerting

document:
# Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Prompt Version Control

Patterns

Where to look What good looks like Platform | Source Control ✅ Store prompt templates in Git alongside application code treating prompts as critical application logic deserving code review, testing, and controlled deployment Einstein | Prompt Builder ✅ Use Prompt Builder for iterative prompt development with version history and testing capabilities, then export to version control for deployment pipelines Platform | Source Control ✅ Store configurations (model selection, temperature, token limits, retrieval configs, action permissions, feature flags) as code enabling environment-specific values and drift detection Platform | Source Control ✅ Apply semantic versioning to agent components: major (breaking changes), minor (features), patch (bug fixes) with version numbers appearing in logs Platform | Documentation ✅ Document what changed, why it changed, what testing validated the change, and what rollback procedures exist for every prompt and configuration change

Anti-Patterns

Where to look What bad looks like Einstein | Prompt Builder ⚠️ Making prompt changes without code review, testing, or controlled deployment processes Platform | Configuration ⚠️ Storing agent configurations outside of source control where drift cannot be detected and deployments cannot be automated Platform | Documentation ⚠️ Making prompt changes without documenting rationale, test results, or rollback procedures Platform | Source Control ⚠️ Failing to apply semantic versioning, making it impossible to correlate incidents with specific deployments

metadata.breadcrumb: Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Prompt Version Control

document:
# Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Model Registry and Deployment Tracking

Patterns

Where to look What good looks like Platform | Documentation ✅ Maintain a model registry recording which model versions are deployed where including model family, specific version, fine-tuning state, environment, deployment date, and responsible team Platform | Documentation ✅ Log every agent deployment including version, environment, timestamp, deploying user, approvals obtained, and deployment outcome Platform | Documentation ✅ Map dependencies between agents, prompts, knowledge bases, actions, and integrations explicitly rather than discovering them during incidents Business | Process ✅ Establish a deprecation schedule with a policy-backed minimum notice period communicated sufficiently in advance, enabling planned migrations rather than emergency responses to forced deprecations Platform | Documentation ✅ Document rollback procedures for each agent including target version, execution steps, validation testing, and notification requirements Platform | Staging ✅ Test rollback procedures in non-production environments validating they work before depending on them during production incidents

Anti-Patterns

Where to look What bad looks like Platform | Documentation ⚠️ Discovering dependencies between agents, prompts, and knowledge bases only during incidents rather than maintaining explicit dependency maps Business | Process ⚠️ Providing insufficient deprecation notice forcing emergency migrations rather than planned transitions Platform | Documentation ⚠️ Having untested rollback procedures that fail when needed most during production incidents Platform | Deployment ⚠️ Deploying agents without logging version, environment, approvals, or outcome, losing ability to correlate incidents with deployments

metadata.breadcrumb: Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Model Registry and Deployment Tracking

document:
# Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Continuous Training and Domain Adaptation (Part 1)

Patterns

Where to look What good looks like Platform | UI ✅ Collect explicit feedback (thumbs up/down, quality scores, comments) and implicit feedback (completion rates, escalation frequencies, retry patterns) systematically Data 360 | Data Curation ✅ Curate conversation logs into training datasets by filtering for quality, removing problematic examples, ensuring representativeness, and deduplicating Data 360 | Grounding ✅ Adapt agents to domain vocabulary, business processes, and organization-specific knowledge primarily through RAG grounded in Data 360 and prompt tuning — the Salesforce-native adaptation path Einstein | BYOLLM ✅ When grounding and prompt tuning are insufficient, fine-tune a model externally and connect it through BYOLLM rather than expecting in-platform generative fine-tuning Einstein | Prompt Builder ✅ Establish regular prompt review cadence examining recent conversations, quality metrics, and user feedback identifying improvement opportunities Einstein | Prompt Builder ✅ Implement prompt changes incrementally with A/B testing validating improvements before full rollout Agentforce | Agent Configuration ✅ Maintain test sets covering happy paths, edge cases, adversarial inputs, and historical problem scenarios, expanding continuously as new edge cases are discovered

Anti-Patterns

metadata.breadcrumb: Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Continuous Training and Domain Adaptation

document:
# Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Continuous Training and Domain Adaptation (Part 2)

Where to look What bad looks like Platform | Data ⚠️ Attempting improvement without systematic feedback collection, making improvement guesswork rather than data-driven Data 360 | Data Curation ⚠️ Using uncurated conversation logs for training including safety violations, errors, and non-representative examples Data 360 | Grounding ⚠️ Reaching for external fine-tuning before exhausting RAG grounding and prompt tuning, the native path that resolves most domain-adaptation needs without a custom model Einstein | Prompt Builder ⚠️ Treating prompt engineering as a one-time exercise rather than continuous practice adjusted as usage patterns evolve Agentforce | Agent Configuration ⚠️ Having static test sets that never expand to cover new edge cases discovered in production

metadata.breadcrumb: Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Continuous Training and Domain Adaptation

document:
# Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Gradual Rollout and A/B Testing (Part 1)

Patterns

Where to look What good looks like Platform | Custom Metadata Types ✅ Implement feature flags using custom metadata types or custom settings to decouple deployment from release for high-risk agent changes Platform | Permission Sets ✅ Implement canary deployments releasing agent changes to a small user subset first using permission sets controlling agent access Agentforce | Agent Configuration ✅ Monitor the canary cohort intensively measuring success rates, quality, error rates, latency, token consumption, and satisfaction, and only expand rollout when the canary matches or improves on the control group running the previous agent version Platform | Analytics ✅ Define success criteria before starting A/B tests preventing ambiguous results, aligned with business objectives Agentforce | Agent Configuration ✅ Deploy champion-challenger testing maintaining proven version as fallback while comparing against improved challenger version Business | Process ✅ Establish objective promotion criteria including minimum sample size, quality thresholds, and evaluation duration before promotion decisions

Anti-Patterns

metadata.breadcrumb: Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Gradual Rollout and A/B Testing

document:
# Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Gradual Rollout and A/B Testing (Part 2)

Where to look What bad looks like Agentforce | Agent Configuration ⚠️ Rolling out agent changes to all users simultaneously without canary testing, maximizing blast radius of issues Platform | Deployment ⚠️ Deploying high-risk agent changes without feature flags enabling instant rollback without redeployment Platform | Analytics ⚠️ Running A/B tests without pre-defined success criteria, leading to ambiguous results and poor decisions Platform | Analytics ⚠️ Running experiments with insufficient sample size producing noisy results that lead to incorrect conclusions Agentforce | Agent Configuration ⚠️ Using feature flags for every minor prompt change rather than reserving them for high-risk changes to business-critical agents

metadata.breadcrumb: Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Gradual Rollout and A/B Testing

document:
# Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Incident Detection and Classification

Patterns

Where to look What good looks like Platform | Monitoring ✅ Detect agent failures through automated monitoring alerting on error rates, quality metric degradation, cost anomalies, latency increases, and user escalations Platform | Monitoring ✅ Supplement automated detection with user reporting mechanisms enabling escalation of issues automated monitoring misses Business | Process ✅ Define severity criteria objectively based on user impact, blast radius, data integrity risk, and recovery urgency Platform | Documentation ✅ Document initial response procedures as runbooks executable by on-call engineers without deep agent expertise Agentforce | Agent Configuration ✅ Include in initial response: disable failing agent (circuit breaker), route to fallback, collect diagnostics, notify stakeholders, initiate incident communication

Anti-Patterns

Where to look What bad looks like Platform | Monitoring ⚠️ Relying on user reports as primary detection mechanism rather than automated monitoring for agent failures Business | Process ⚠️ Using subjective severity classification that leads to under-escalating real problems or over-escalating minor issues Platform | Documentation ⚠️ Having no runbooks, requiring incident-specific investigation by engineers with deep agent expertise during every incident Business | Process ⚠️ Treating agent failures identically to traditional application failures without accounting for hallucinations, off-topic responses, or safety violations

metadata.breadcrumb: Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Incident Detection and Classification

document:
# Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Circuit Breakers and Fallback (Part 1)

Patterns

Where to look What good looks like Platform | Apex ✅ Implement circuit breakers with configurable error threshold (e.g., 50% error rate), duration window (e.g., 5 min rolling window), and recovery testing (periodic trial requests) Agentforce | Agent Configuration ✅ Design fallback hierarchies: Primary sophisticated agent → Simpler backup agent → Static FAQ responses → Human handoff Platform | Orchestration ✅ Implement fallback logic in orchestration layer rather than within individual agents enabling consistent behavior across agent ecosystem Agentforce | Agent Configuration ✅ Design human handoff workflows preserving conversation context, communicating handoff reason, and routing to appropriate human agent with relevant expertise Platform | Monitoring ✅ Monitor handoff rates by topic, agent, and failure reason to identify agent capability gaps Agentforce | Agent Configuration ✅ When sophisticated reasoning fails, fallback to simpler logic; when real-time data unavailable, operate on cached data; when integrations fail, operate in read-only mode Platform | Orchestration ✅ Test fallback paths regularly validating they work when needed

Anti-Patterns

metadata.breadcrumb: Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Circuit Breakers and Fallback

document:
# Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Circuit Breakers and Fallback (Part 2)

Where to look What bad looks like Agentforce | Agent Configuration ⚠️ Having no circuit breakers, allowing failing agents to repeatedly impact users while issues are resolved Platform | Orchestration ⚠️ Implementing fallback logic within individual agents rather than at the orchestration layer, creating inconsistent behavior Agentforce | Agent Configuration ⚠️ Designing binary pass/fail agents that either work perfectly or completely fail without graceful degradation options Platform | Orchestration ⚠️ Never testing fallback paths, discovering they don’t work only during actual incidents Agentforce | Agent Configuration ⚠️ Human handoff that loses conversation context forcing users to repeat information

metadata.breadcrumb: Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Circuit Breakers and Fallback

document:
# Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Post-Incident Analysis (Part 1)

Patterns

Where to look What good looks like Business | Process ✅ Conduct blameless post-incident reviews focusing on system improvements rather than individual fault creating psychological safety Business | Process ✅ Create detailed timeline from initial conditions through detection, investigation, response, recovery, and validation with timestamps Business | Process ✅ Use “Five Whys” technique drilling from symptoms to fundamental causes rather than simplistic conclusions Business | Process ✅ Analyze contributing factors including monitoring gaps, testing gaps, documentation gaps, automation gaps, and architectural gaps Business | Process ✅ Evaluate detection: what signal should have detected problem earlier, what monitoring enables faster detection Business | Process ✅ Specify concrete, assigned, timebound action items preventing recurrence (e.g., “add alert for error rate exceeding 5% over 10min - assigned: Alex - due: 2 weeks”) Business | Process ✅ Track action item completion in subsequent reviews ensuring continuous improvement actually happens Platform | Documentation ✅ Document post-incident reviews in shared knowledge base with tagging enabling pattern analysis across multiple incidents Business | Process ✅ Share post-incident reviews broadly beyond immediate incident responders through team meetings or lunch-and-learn sessions

Anti-Patterns

metadata.breadcrumb: Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Post-Incident Analysis

document:
# Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Post-Incident Analysis (Part 2)

Where to look What bad looks like Business | Process ⚠️ Blame-focused postmortems that reduce psychological safety and prevent honest assessment of failures Business | Process ⚠️ Simplistic root cause conclusions (“the agent had a bug”) rather than specific findings enabling effective remediation Business | Process ⚠️ Vague action items like “improve monitoring” instead of specific, assigned, timebound tasks Business | Process ⚠️ Low action item completion rates indicating continuous improvement process failure Business | Process ⚠️ Keeping post-incident learnings siloed to immediate responders rather than sharing broadly for organizational learning

metadata.breadcrumb: Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Post-Incident Analysis

document:
# Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Deployment Approval

Patterns

Where to look What good looks like Business | Process ✅ Validate pre-deployment checklist including testing, security review, compliance validation, documentation, monitoring configuration, and stakeholder approval Business | Process ✅ Evaluate risk based on blast radius, data sensitivity, action authority, integration dependencies, recovery complexity, and compliance implications Business | Process ✅ Scale approval requirements based on risk: high-risk requires executive approval, security review, and gradual rollout; low-risk requires peer review and standard testing Platform | Approval Processes ✅ Implement automated, tracked, and auditable approval workflows using Salesforce approval processes or external deployment tools Business | Process ✅ Define emergency bypass procedures requiring executive approval, rationale documentation, and expedited post-deployment review Platform | Monitoring ✅ Track emergency deployments separately; high emergency deployment frequency indicates process problems requiring investigation

Anti-Patterns

Where to look What bad looks like Business | Process ⚠️ Applying uniform approval depth regardless of agent risk profile, wasting effort on low-risk agents or under-reviewing high-risk ones Business | Process ⚠️ Deploying production agents without pre-deployment checklist validation of testing, security, compliance, and monitoring Platform | Deployment ⚠️ Having no emergency bypass procedures, causing critical fix delays during production incidents Business | Process ⚠️ Frequently requiring emergency deployments, indicating broken standard processes rather than exceptional circumstances

metadata.breadcrumb: Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Deployment Approval

document:
# Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Quality Gates and Testing (Part 1)

Patterns

Where to look What good looks like Agentforce | Agent Configuration ✅ Test output characteristics (contains required information, maintains appropriate tone, includes citations) rather than exact text for non-deterministic agent outputs Agentforce | Agent Configuration ✅ Establish minimum quality thresholds (e.g., “95% accuracy on held-out test set, zero safety violations, fairness audit shows no demographic disparities exceeding 5%“) Agentforce | Agent Configuration ✅ Perform safety testing with adversarial inputs including prompt injection, jailbreak attempts, request escalation, and out-of-scope requests Agentforce | Agent Configuration ✅ Have safety testing performed by team members not involved in agent development providing fresh perspective on vulnerabilities Platform | Performance Testing ✅ Test under realistic load including concurrent conversations, typical conversation lengths, and projected usage volume Platform | Security ✅ Validate that agents cannot access unauthorized data, cannot perform unauthorized actions, and that prompt injection cannot escalate privileges Platform | CI/CD ✅ Integrate security scanning in deployment pipeline using Salesforce Code Analyzer and specialized AI security tools

Anti-Patterns

metadata.breadcrumb: Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Quality Gates and Testing

document:
# Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Quality Gates and Testing (Part 2)

Where to look What bad looks like Agentforce | Agent Configuration ⚠️ Testing agents for exact text match on non-deterministic outputs rather than testing output characteristics Platform | Performance Testing ⚠️ Only testing with single-user scenarios, missing governor limit issues, resource constraints, and scalability bottlenecks Agentforce | Agent Configuration ⚠️ Skipping safety testing or having developers test their own agents without fresh perspective on vulnerabilities Platform | Security ⚠️ Not testing whether prompt injection can escalate agent privileges or access unauthorized data Agentforce | Agent Configuration ⚠️ Having static test sets that don’t represent real usage diversity including different user types and conversation complexities

metadata.breadcrumb: Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Quality Gates and Testing

document:
# Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Change Management

Patterns

Where to look What good looks like Platform | Documentation ✅ Document every change: what changed, why, what testing validated it, and what rollback procedure exists Business | Communication ✅ Notify all stakeholders (users, ops teams, support, business) describing what is changing, when, what benefits, what risks, and who to contact Business | Communication ✅ Establish communication templates for different change types standardizing messages and reducing preparation overhead Platform | Event Monitoring ✅ Time agent deployments during low-usage periods informed by Event Monitoring data showing actual usage patterns Business | Process ✅ Deploy major agent changes early to midweek avoiding weekends with reduced incident response capability Business | Process ✅ Establish change freeze periods before major business events (fiscal year end, product launches, major marketing campaigns) Business | Process ✅ Document change freeze calendar annually communicating restricted periods sufficiently in advance

Anti-Patterns

Where to look What bad looks like Platform | Deployment ⚠️ Deploying during peak usage, month-end close, quarter-end close, or major business events Platform | Deployment ⚠️ Deploying on Mondays (ramping up) or Fridays (reduced staffing) when incident response capability is limited Business | Process ⚠️ Having excessive change freezes that slow improvement velocity without proportionate risk reduction Business | Communication ⚠️ Deploying agent changes without notifying affected users, operations teams, support teams, or business stakeholders Platform | Documentation ⚠️ Making changes without documenting rationale, creating organizations that rediscover lessons rather than building on experience

metadata.breadcrumb: Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Change Management

document:
# Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Feedback Loop Architecture

Patterns

Where to look What good looks like Platform | UI ✅ Implement feedback collection within conversation UI enabling immediate response while interaction is fresh rather than delayed collection Platform | Analytics ✅ Query conversation logs analyzing question types, conversation lengths, success rates by topic, and user satisfaction by conversation characteristics Platform | Analytics ✅ Analyze error logs grouping by error type, affected users, conversation patterns, and temporal distribution to reveal systematic issues Platform | Analytics ✅ Prioritize error remediation by frequency and impact: high-frequency errors affecting many users warrant immediate attention Platform | Monitoring ✅ Establish quality baselines after initial deployment and monitor ongoing quality against baselines alerting when trends decline

Anti-Patterns

Where to look What bad looks like Platform | UI ⚠️ Delaying feedback collection (e.g., follow-up emails days later) reducing response rates and introducing recall bias Platform | Analytics ⚠️ Not analyzing usage patterns to determine whether agents justify operational complexity or whether capabilities are underutilized Platform | Analytics ⚠️ Treating all errors equally rather than prioritizing by frequency and business impact Platform | Monitoring ⚠️ Making improvement decisions without data, lacking quality baselines and trend monitoring

metadata.breadcrumb: Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Feedback Loop Architecture

document:
# Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Experiment Tracking

Patterns

Where to look What good looks like Business | Process ✅ Provide consistent experiment structure: hypothesis, experimental design, metrics, sample size, and success criteria Business | Process ✅ Document experiments before execution preventing ambiguous interpretation of results Platform | Analytics ✅ Track variant assignment in conversation metadata enabling outcome correlation by variant Platform | Analytics ✅ Calculate required sample size before experiments based on expected effect size, statistical power, and acceptable error rates Platform | Analytics ✅ Use multi-armed bandit optimization to dynamically allocate more traffic to better-performing variants reducing opportunity cost Platform | Documentation ✅ Maintain experiment catalog with variants tested, outcomes measured, results achieved, and decisions made to prevent retesting failed approaches

Anti-Patterns

Where to look What bad looks like Business | Process ⚠️ Running experiments without pre-defined hypotheses and success criteria leading to ambiguous results Platform | Analytics ⚠️ Using insufficient sample sizes producing noisy results that lead to poor improvement decisions Platform | Documentation ⚠️ Having no experiment catalog, causing teams to retest previously failed approaches and lose organizational knowledge Platform | Analytics ⚠️ Not tracking which users received which variants, making outcome correlation impossible

metadata.breadcrumb: Operational Excellence - Agentic Patterns > Experiment Tracking

Learn more about Well-Architected Operational Excellence → Incident Management

document:
# Incident Management - Patterns > Incident Detection and Alerting (Part 1)

Patterns

Where to look What good looks like Platform | Monitoring ✅ Alerting architecture includes severity classification routing critical incidents (production unavailable, data corruption, security compromise) to page on-call immediately Platform | Monitoring ✅ High severity incidents (degraded performance, partial outage) generate immediate notifications for prompt business-hours investigation Platform | Monitoring ✅ Warnings (approaching thresholds, configuration drift) aggregate into daily digest for proactive remediation Platform | Monitoring ✅ Alert enrichment includes diagnostic context: affected user count, error rate percentiles, recent deployments, related alerts, and direct dashboard links Platform | Monitoring ✅ Alert context reduces mean time to acknowledge by providing immediate situation assessment without gathering basic information through separate queries Platform | Monitoring ✅ Alert grouping prevents alert storms by consolidating hundreds of related alerts from single underlying problem into one notification with aggregate statistics Platform | Monitoring ✅ Grouped alerts show count, rate, and affected transactions revealing problem pattern without overwhelming responders Platform | Monitoring ✅ Alert suppression prevents known-transient conditions from generating alerts during expected maintenance windows or auto-remediation periods

Anti-Patterns

metadata.breadcrumb: Incident Management - Patterns > Incident Detection and Alerting

document:
# Incident Management - Patterns > Incident Detection and Alerting (Part 2)

Where to look What bad looks like Platform | Monitoring ⚠️ Integration failure generates 100s individual alerts in 5 minutes overwhelming on-call phone, each alert identical except timestamp Platform | Monitoring ⚠️ Alerts lack context about scope, recent changes, or problem patterns; on-call engineer must gather basic information manually Platform | Monitoring ⚠️ All alerts route through same channel regardless of severity; critical production outages compete with minor warnings Platform | Monitoring ⚠️ Alerts fire during scheduled maintenance windows generating false positives that erode trust in monitoring system Platform | Monitoring ⚠️ Alert grouping does not exist; each transaction failure fires separate alert creating alert storms during incidents Platform | Monitoring ⚠️ Alerts provide no links to relevant dashboards; responders spend time finding monitoring tools during incident response

metadata.breadcrumb: Incident Management - Patterns > Incident Detection and Alerting

document:
# Incident Management - Patterns > On-Call Rotation and Runbook (Part 1)

Patterns

Where to look What good looks like Platform | Operations ✅ On-call rotation is weekly or bi-weekly balancing burden distribution against context preservation Platform | Operations ✅ Runbooks are documented for every alert type enabling on-call engineers to respond effectively without deep domain expertise Platform | Operations ✅ Runbooks include problem description, diagnostic steps, remediation procedures, escalation criteria, and related documentation links Platform | Operations ✅ Runbooks are living documents in version control that evolve through postmortem action items Platform | Operations ✅ Handoff procedures include brief meetings during rotation transitions transferring context including active issues, recent changes, known risks, and upcoming maintenance Platform | Operations ✅ Written handoff notes supplement verbal handoff preventing information loss during rotation transitions Platform | Operations ✅ Page frequency, after-hours incident count, and false positive rate are measured to identify unsustainable on-call burden requiring architectural remediation

Anti-Patterns

metadata.breadcrumb: Incident Management - Patterns > On-Call Rotation and Runbook

document:
# Incident Management - Patterns > On-Call Rotation and Runbook (Part 2)

Where to look What bad looks like Platform | Operations ⚠️ Runbooks do not exist; on-call engineers rely on tribal knowledge and frequent escalations to subject matter experts Platform | Operations ⚠️ Runbooks are stored in personal documents rather than shared version control where team members can access and update them Platform | Operations ⚠️ On-call rotation transitions happen without handoff meetings; incoming engineer lacks context about active issues and recent changes Platform | Operations ⚠️ High on-call burden continues indefinitely through operational heroics rather than driving architectural improvements Platform | Operations ⚠️ On-call metrics (page frequency, after-hours incidents, false positives) are not tracked; burden patterns remain invisible Platform | Operations ⚠️ Runbooks are created once during initial deployment and never updated as system evolves or new failure modes emerge

metadata.breadcrumb: Incident Management - Patterns > On-Call Rotation and Runbook

document:
# Incident Management - Patterns > Escalation Path

Patterns

Where to look What good looks like Platform | Operations ✅ Technical escalation paths define which subject matter experts handle specific problem domains Platform | Operations ✅ Management escalation paths define which managers receive notification for incidents exceeding severity or duration thresholds Platform | Operations ✅ Vendor escalation paths document Salesforce support case creation procedures and severity criteria Platform | Operations ✅ Executive escalation paths define which executives receive notification for business-critical incidents Platform | Operations ✅ Escalation criteria are explicit and objective: severity levels, time thresholds, affected user counts, business impact assessments Platform | Operations ✅ Escalation paths are documented in runbooks and accessible during incidents without searching for contact information

Anti-Patterns

Where to look What bad looks like Platform | Operations ⚠️ Escalation paths are not documented; on-call engineers waste time searching for appropriate contacts during incidents Platform | Operations ⚠️ Escalation criteria are vague (“escalate if it seems bad”); responders lack clear guidance about when to escalate Platform | Operations ⚠️ Management notification happens too late because severity thresholds are undefined; executives learn about incidents from users Platform | Operations ⚠️ Salesforce support escalation procedures are not documented; teams delay opening support cases losing valuable response time Platform | Operations ⚠️ Subject matter expert contacts are outdated; escalations reach wrong people or fail during rotation changes

metadata.breadcrumb: Incident Management - Patterns > Escalation Path

document:
# Incident Management - Patterns > Post-Incident Review Process (Part 1)

Patterns

metadata.breadcrumb: Incident Management - Patterns > Post-Incident Review Process

document:
# Incident Management - Patterns > Post-Incident Review Process (Part 2)

Where to look What good looks like Platform | Operations ✅ Blameless post-incident reviews are conducted within 5 business days after significant operational events Platform | Operations ✅ Blameless culture focuses on system improvements rather than individual blame, creating psychological safety for honest assessment Platform | Operations ✅ Timeline includes detailed sequence from initial conditions through first signal, detection, acknowledgment, investigation, response, recovery, and validation Platform | Operations ✅ Timeline timestamps each event enabling duration analysis of detection, response, and recovery phases Platform | Operations ✅ Root cause identifies technical failure or condition that directly caused incident, distinguished from contributing factors Platform | Operations ✅ Contributing factors analysis reveals organizational, process, or architectural conditions that enabled or amplified incident impact Platform | Operations ✅ Detection analysis evaluates how incident was detected and whether detection could have been faster Platform | Operations ✅ Response evaluation identifies what went well during response and what was slower or harder than necessary Platform | Operations ✅ Action items are specific, assigned, and timebound preventing recurrence or improving future response Platform | Operations ✅ Action items avoid vague improvements (“improve monitoring”) in favor of concrete tasks (“add alert for API error rate exceeding 5% over 10min window”)

metadata.breadcrumb: Incident Management - Patterns > Post-Incident Review Process

document:
# Incident Management - Patterns > Post-Incident Review Process (Part 3)

Anti-Patterns

Where to look What bad looks like Platform | Operations ⚠️ Post-incident discussion concludes “batch job had a bug, we fixed it” with no documentation or systematic improvements Platform | Operations ⚠️ Post-incident reviews focus on individual fault rather than system improvements, destroying psychological safety Platform | Operations ⚠️ Timeline lacks timestamps preventing duration analysis; team cannot identify whether detection or response was slow Platform | Operations ⚠️ Root cause analysis does not distinguish immediate technical cause from organizational or process contributing factors Platform | Operations ⚠️ Detection analysis is skipped; monitoring gaps that allowed users to report incident first are not identified Platform | Operations ⚠️ Action items are vague without owners or due dates; improvements are discussed but never implemented Platform | Operations ⚠️ Post-incident reviews are not conducted within 5 business days; context is lost and urgency for improvements fades

metadata.breadcrumb: Incident Management - Patterns > Post-Incident Review Process

document:
# Incident Management - Patterns > Post-Incident Documentation and Learning (Part 1)

Patterns

Where to look What good looks like Platform | Knowledge Management ✅ Post-incident reviews are documented and shared broadly beyond immediate incident responders for organizational learning Platform | Knowledge Management ✅ Post-incident reviews are stored in shared wiki or knowledge base with tagging enabling pattern analysis across multiple incidents Platform | Knowledge Management ✅ Action item completion is tracked in subsequent reviews preventing retrospectives from becoming repetitive discussion without follow-through Platform | Knowledge Management ✅ Action item completion rates are measured as operational health indicator revealing whether improvements are implemented or merely discussed Platform | Operations ✅ Incident patterns are analyzed across multiple incidents revealing systemic issues requiring architectural investment Platform | Operations ✅ Runbooks are updated based on post-incident learnings ensuring procedures reflect actual incident response experience

Anti-Patterns

metadata.breadcrumb: Incident Management - Patterns > Post-Incident Documentation and Learning

document:
# Incident Management - Patterns > Post-Incident Documentation and Learning (Part 2)

Where to look What bad looks like Platform | Knowledge Management ⚠️ Post-incident reviews are not documented; learnings remain with incident responders rather than spreading across organization Platform | Knowledge Management ⚠️ Post-incident reviews are stored in personal documents rather than shared knowledge base where team members can learn from history Platform | Knowledge Management ⚠️ Action items are defined but never tracked; completion rate is unknown and improvements are not implemented Platform | Knowledge Management ⚠️ Low action item completion rates persist without recognition that retrospectives are ineffective without follow-through Platform | Operations ⚠️ Incident patterns are not analyzed across multiple incidents; systemic issues remain hidden because each incident is treated in isolation Platform | Operations ⚠️ Runbooks are not updated after incidents; procedures become outdated as system evolves and new failure modes emerge

metadata.breadcrumb: Incident Management - Patterns > Post-Incident Documentation and Learning

document:
# Incident Management - Patterns > Incident Metrics and Monitoring (Part 1)

Patterns

Where to look What good looks like Platform | Operations ✅ Mean time to detect (MTTD) is tracked measuring duration from incident occurrence to detection Platform | Operations ✅ Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) is tracked measuring duration from detection to on-call engineer acknowledgment Platform | Operations ✅ Mean time to restore (MTTR) is tracked measuring duration from detection to service restoration Platform | Operations ✅ Incident frequency is tracked with monthly trend review revealing whether stability is improving or degrading Platform | Operations ✅ Change failure rate is tracked measuring percentage of deployments causing production incidents requiring remediation Platform | Operations ✅ Change failure rate is kept consistently low, a small fraction of all deployments Platform | Operations ✅ Incident metrics are shared with development teams during sprint planning informing backlog prioritization and architectural improvements

Anti-Patterns

metadata.breadcrumb: Incident Management - Patterns > Incident Metrics and Monitoring

document:
# Incident Management - Patterns > Incident Metrics and Monitoring (Part 2)

Where to look What bad looks like Platform | Operations ⚠️ Incident metrics are not tracked; team has no visibility into whether response times are improving or degrading Platform | Operations ⚠️ MTTD, MTTA, and MTTR are not measured; teams cannot identify whether detection or response is the bottleneck Platform | Operations ⚠️ Change failure rate is not tracked; team does not know whether quality gates are effective Platform | Operations ⚠️ Incident frequency trends are not reviewed monthly; stability degradation is not detected until major incident occurs Platform | Operations ⚠️ Incident metrics remain in operations team without sharing to development teams; architectural problems are not addressed Platform | Operations ⚠️ Metrics are tracked but never used to inform decisions; measurement without action wastes effort and provides no value

metadata.breadcrumb: Incident Management - Patterns > Incident Metrics and Monitoring

# Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Observability and Monitoring - Patterns

Learn more about Well-Architected Operational Excellence → Observability and Monitoring

metadata.breadcrumb: Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Observability and Monitoring - Patterns

document:
# Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Observability Framework (Part 1)

Patterns

Where to look What good looks like Platform | Event Monitoring ✅ Event Monitoring is designed into initial architecture capturing correlation IDs that trace requests through async processing chains and external integrations Platform | Event Monitoring ✅ Observability infrastructure is included from initial sprint rather than retrofitted after production incidents prove impossible to diagnose Platform | Integration ✅ Integration checkpoints are placed deliberately to enable request tracing across system boundaries Platform | Platform Events ✅ Platform Event payloads are structured for operational visibility with transaction markers and context Platform | Custom Logging ✅ Custom logging framework captures discrete events with full contextual information including user identity, timestamp, duration, and outcome Platform | Metrics ✅ Metrics aggregate numerical measurements over time revealing trends including API consumption rates, Apex CPU time distributions, and batch job success rates Platform | Distributed Tracing ✅ Traces connect synchronous API calls to asynchronous processing chains, platform events to subscriber executions, and integration requests to external system responses Platform | Observability ✅ Observability enables operators to answer arbitrary questions about system behavior without deploying new instrumentation for each investigation

Anti-Patterns

metadata.breadcrumb: Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Observability Framework

document:
# Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Observability Framework (Part 2)

Where to look What bad looks like Platform | Event Monitoring ⚠️ Solution launches without custom logging, requiring major refactoring six months later when production incidents prove impossible to diagnose with platform logs alone Platform | Event Monitoring ⚠️ Observability is retrofitted into existing solution requiring instrumentation changes touching most components and risking bugs during operational improvement work Platform | Integration ⚠️ Integration failures occur but request paths cannot be traced across system boundaries without comprehensive telemetry Platform | Platform Events ⚠️ Platform Event payloads lack operational context making incident investigation dependent on searching multiple systems Platform | Custom Logging ⚠️ Logs capture insufficient context; investigations require reproducing issues to gather additional information Platform | Observability ⚠️ Predefined dashboards cannot answer unexpected questions about system behavior emerging in production

metadata.breadcrumb: Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Observability Framework

document:
# Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Platform Health Monitoring (Part 1)

Patterns

metadata.breadcrumb: Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Platform Health Monitoring

document:
# Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Platform Health Monitoring (Part 2)

Where to look What good looks like Platform | Event Monitoring ✅ Event Monitoring is enabled for production environments capturing API usage, login activity, Apex execution, SOQL queries, Visualforce pages, Lightning pages, and report runs Platform | Event Monitoring ✅ Event Log Files export hourly to centralized log platform enabling historical analysis beyond native platform retention Platform | Event Monitoring ✅ External log aggregation enables correlation with enterprise telemetry from other systems for end-to-end transaction tracing Platform | Event Monitoring ✅ Event Log Files are retained matching regulatory requirements for compliance reporting and long-term trend analysis Platform | Proactive Monitoring ✅ Proactive Monitoring thresholds are tuned deliberately based on org-specific normal operating range rather than accepting defaults Platform | Proactive Monitoring ✅ Proactive Monitoring alerts detect API limit spikes, concurrent Apex failures, SOQL row limit approaches, and row lock contention before user-visible incidents Platform | Proactive Monitoring ✅ Tuned thresholds generate actionable signals that teams trust and act on creating virtuous cycles of continuous improvement Platform | Scale Center ✅ Scale Center baselines are established during solution stabilization and revisited after each major release Platform | Scale Center ✅ Scale Center reveals which operations consume the most resources, which transactions approach timeout thresholds, and where optimization investment yields greatest impact Platform | Scale Center ✅ Transaction time increases from baseline prompt investigation revealing unintentional N+1 query patterns introduced in latest deployment Platform | Setup Audit Trail ✅ Setup Audit Trail tracks configuration changes including permission modifications, metadata deployments, and security setting updates with retention up to 180 days Platform | Setup Audit Trail ✅ Setup Audit Trail entries are exported for retention beyond 180 days when compliance or contractual requirements demand longer historical windows Platform | Shield ✅ Field Audit Trail is enabled selectively for fields containing sensitive data, regulated data requiring change history, or critical business data Platform | Shield ✅ Field Audit Trail provides up to 10 years retention for fields where understanding historical values aids operations and compliance reporting Platform | Health Check ✅ Health Check reviews are scheduled quarterly with findings remediated based on risk prioritization for the environment Platform | Health Check ✅ Health Check findings receive deliberate review rather than passive acceptance; compensating controls or different risk tolerances are documented

metadata.breadcrumb: Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Platform Health Monitoring

document:
# Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Platform Health Monitoring (Part 3)

Anti-Patterns

metadata.breadcrumb: Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Platform Health Monitoring

document:
# Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Platform Health Monitoring (Part 4)

Where to look What bad looks like Platform | Event Monitoring ⚠️ Event Monitoring is enabled but logs are never exported, limiting investigations to the native retention window and preventing historical trend analysis Platform | Event Monitoring ⚠️ Event Log Files remain in platform storage; external aggregation is not implemented preventing long-term capacity planning Platform | Proactive Monitoring ⚠️ Proactive Monitoring uses default thresholds that are too sensitive or too lax, generating noisy alerts that teams learn to ignore Platform | Proactive Monitoring ⚠️ Alert noise destroys trust in monitoring system; teams stop responding to valid signals Platform | Scale Center ⚠️ Scale Center is enabled but never reviewed proactively; performance slowly degrades until users complain after months of incremental degradation Platform | Scale Center ⚠️ Performance metrics lack baseline context; unclear whether 3-second transaction times are typical, improving, or degrading Platform | Setup Audit Trail ⚠️ Setup Audit Trail is not exported; retention limitations prevent security investigations or compliance validation beyond 180 days Platform | Shield ⚠️ Field Audit Trail is enabled for all fields rather than selectively, creating storage costs without corresponding compliance value Platform | Health Check ⚠️ Health Check findings are never reviewed; security configuration drifts from baseline recommendations without deliberate acceptance

metadata.breadcrumb: Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Platform Health Monitoring

# Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Application and Integration Monitoring (Part 1)

Patterns

metadata.breadcrumb: Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Application and Integration Monitoring

document:
# Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Application and Integration Monitoring (Part 2)

Where to look What good looks like Platform | User Flows ✅ Critical user flows are defined based on business impact and monitored end-to-end for success rates, completion time, abandonment points, and error rates Platform | User Flows ✅ Critical flows include revenue-generating activities (order submission, contract execution, opportunity close), high-volume activities (login, search, record creation), and compliance-required activities (consent capture, data subject rights fulfillment) Platform | User Flows ✅ Flows are instrumented with transaction markers indicating start, completion, abandonment, and failure at each significant step Platform | User Flows ✅ Order submission flow instrumented with platform events at each stage (cart validation, inventory check, payment processing, fulfillment trigger) showing success rate by stage Platform | User Flows ✅ Flow-level monitoring reveals problems invisible in component-level monitoring because failures can occur at any transition point Platform | User Flows ✅ Alerts fire when flow success rates drop below acceptable thresholds or duration exceeds latency targets Platform | Integration ✅ Integration health monitoring detects external system failures, network issues, authentication problems, and rate limit approaches before cascading into user-facing failures Platform | Integration ✅ Success rate monitoring alerts when falling below 99% for critical synchronous integrations Platform | Integration ✅ Error distribution monitoring alerts when new error types appear that did not exist in baseline Platform | Integration ✅ Latency percentile monitoring (p95) alerts when exceeding 3 seconds for synchronous user-facing calls Platform | Integration ✅ Throughput monitoring alerts when above 80% of known rate limit or SLA threshold Platform | Integration ✅ Circuit breaker state monitoring alerts when any circuit opens indicating external system degradation Platform | Integration ✅ Retry rate monitoring alerts when sustained retry rate exceeds 5% indicating reliability issues Platform | Integration ✅ Integration telemetry routes to centralized monitoring platforms enabling correlation across system boundaries

metadata.breadcrumb: Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Application and Integration Monitoring

document:
# Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Application and Integration Monitoring (Part 3)

Anti-Patterns

Where to look What bad looks like Platform | User Flows ⚠️ Components are monitored independently showing healthy operation while 12% of users abandon critical flows with no visibility into why Platform | User Flows ⚠️ Component health dashboards show green while users cannot complete critical workflows revealing monitoring architecture failure Platform | User Flows ⚠️ User journey touching multiple Apex classes, flows, platform events, and external integrations lacks end-to-end visibility Platform | User Flows ⚠️ Critical business journeys lack instrumentation; success rates and abandonment points are unknown Platform | Integration ⚠️ Integration failures are detected only after cascading into user-facing failures rather than proactively Platform | Integration ⚠️ Integration telemetry remains isolated in individual systems preventing correlation and root cause analysis across boundaries Platform | Integration ⚠️ Monitoring alerts on downstream symptoms after damage is done rather than revealing root causes early

metadata.breadcrumb: Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Application and Integration Monitoring

# Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Service Level Indicators and Objectives (Part 1)

Patterns

metadata.breadcrumb: Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Service Level Indicators and Objectives

document:
# Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Service Level Indicators and Objectives (Part 2)

Where to look What good looks like Platform | SLIs ✅ Availability SLIs measure percentage of time critical flows execute successfully from user perspective (receiving expected result, not just 200 status code) Platform | SLIs ✅ Latency SLIs measure time to complete operations at p50 (median), p90 (90th percentile excluding outliers), p95 (95th percentile excluding worst outliers), and p99 (99th percentile showing worst-case experience) Platform | SLIs ✅ Latency targets vary by operation criticality and user expectation (500ms search feels instantaneous, same latency for typing input feels sluggish) Platform | SLIs ✅ Throughput SLIs measure volume of successful operations per time unit revealing capacity utilization and growth trends Platform | SLIs ✅ Throughput combined with latency reveals whether system maintains performance under increasing load or degrades as volume grows Platform | SLIs ✅ Error rate SLIs distinguish between error types (user errors like validation failures versus system errors like governor limit exceptions) Platform | SLOs ✅ Service Level Objectives are established defining acceptable SLI thresholds based on business requirements before selecting architecture patterns Platform | SLOs ✅ Business requirement “Sales reps must see opportunity updates within 5 seconds” drives SLO “Opportunity detail page loads complete within 3 seconds at p95” which drives architecture decisions Platform | SLOs ✅ SLOs emerge from business requirements and drive architectural decisions rather than being defined based on what system currently achieves

metadata.breadcrumb: Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Service Level Indicators and Objectives

document:
# Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Service Level Indicators and Objectives (Part 3)

Anti-Patterns

Where to look What bad looks like Platform | SLIs ⚠️ Availability is measured from technical perspective (200 status code) rather than user perspective (receiving expected result) Platform | SLIs ⚠️ Latency is measured only at median without understanding worst-case user experience at p95 or p99 percentiles Platform | SLIs ⚠️ Error rate SLIs do not distinguish between user errors and system errors, masking different problems requiring different solutions Platform | SLOs ⚠️ Architecture is built first, then SLO is defined as “whatever we currently achieve” leading to acceptance of 12-second page loads because system design never considered user requirements Platform | SLOs ⚠️ SLOs are architecture-driven rather than business-driven, setting targets based on what system achieves rather than what users need

metadata.breadcrumb: Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Service Level Indicators and Objectives

# Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Alerting Architecture (Part 1)

Patterns

metadata.breadcrumb: Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Alerting Architecture

document:
# Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Alerting Architecture (Part 2)

Where to look What good looks like Platform | Alerting ✅ Severity classification routes critical incidents (production unavailable, data corruption risk, security compromise) to page on-call engineers immediately Platform | Alerting ✅ High severity incidents (degraded performance, partial outages) generate notifications for prompt investigation within business hours Platform | Alerting ✅ Warnings (approaching thresholds, configuration drift) generate daily digest notifications for proactive remediation Platform | Alerting ✅ Alert context includes affected user count, error messages, stack traces, recent deployments, related alerts, and links to relevant dashboards Platform | Alerting ✅ Rich context reduces mean time to acknowledge by enabling immediate severity assessment and investigation without gathering basic information Platform | Alerting ✅ Alert grouping prevents alert storms where hundreds of related alerts fire for single underlying problem Platform | Alerting ✅ Integration failure triggers one alert grouped by integration endpoint showing 156 failed requests in past 5 minutes with latency graph, error distribution, and dashboard link Platform | Alerting ✅ Alert suppression prevents known-transient conditions from generating alerts during expected maintenance windows or auto-remediation periods Platform | Alerting ✅ Alerts are suppressed during scheduled maintenance, during first few minutes after deployment while caches warm, and during brief transient failures where retry logic succeeds

metadata.breadcrumb: Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Alerting Architecture

document:
# Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Alerting Architecture (Part 3)

Anti-Patterns

Where to look What bad looks like Platform | Alerting ⚠️ All alerts route to same channel without severity classification; critical incidents are not distinguished from routine warnings Platform | Alerting ⚠️ Alerts lack diagnostic context; on-call engineers must gather basic information through separate queries before assessing severity Platform | Alerting ⚠️ Integration failure generates 156 individual alerts in 5 minutes overwhelming on-call engineer’s phone, each alert identical except for timestamp Platform | Alerting ⚠️ Alert storms prevent responders from distinguishing single underlying problem from hundreds of related symptoms Platform | Alerting ⚠️ Alerts fire during known maintenance windows and transient conditions generating noise that erodes trust in monitoring Platform | Alerting ⚠️ Alert fatigue from noisy false positives causes teams to ignore notifications reducing response effectiveness

metadata.breadcrumb: Observability and Monitoring - Patterns > Alerting Architecture
